Subject: Re: Crestview pilot – redlines attached; guidance needed on cap & warranty

Marissa — I reviewed the attachments and summarized the material legal risks below. My recommendation is at the end.

Summary of redlines:
- Liability cap: customer proposed $5M uncapped by any carveouts; our standard cap is $1M, policy allows up to $2M with VP approval.
- Warranty: customer asks to carve out warranty obligations for data supplied or controlled by them and for certain integrations; their language is broad and would effectively eliminate our warranty remedies for the very failures we need to remedy.
- Indemnity: their edits expand customer indemnities for privacy incidents and attempt to shift broader notification/forensics obligations to us.

Legal risk & practical impact:
- Increasing the cap to $5M materially raises our downside exposure, particularly for a pilot where we have limited telemetry on stability and integration complexity.
- A broad warranty carveout reduces our leverage and could leave us with no contractual recourse for issues that originate in our runtime.
- The expanded indemnity tied to privacy incidents is manageable only if we can (a) narrow scope to breaches caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and (b) maintain control of defense and settlement.

Proposed legal counter (short form):
- Cap: Counter to a $3M cap for this 12-month pilot only, with an explicit auto-revert to standard $1M cap on renewal.
- Warranty: Accept a narrowly tailored carveout that excludes warranties only to the extent a failure was directly caused by customer-supplied third-party data and not by Redwood services or integrations we provide.
- Indemnity: Retain Redwood's right to defend/settle; limit indemnity to incidents arising from Redwood's breach of representations or Redwood's gross negligence/willful misconduct; exclude indirect/consequential damages to the extent allowed by law.

Why escalate: The $3M counter is above Deal Desk policy ($2M). If the commercial team wants to accept Crestview's economic asks (requested discount + higher cap) we need exec approval because the combination materially changes our unit economics and increases risk.

Attachments: I attached a short redline (proposed-legal-redline.docx) with the language above and a one-page risk note. If you want to proceed with the $3M pilot-cap + limited warranty carveout, we need (1) an explicit business rationale and (2) exec sign-off on the cap and commercial concessions.

Suggested approval path: Laura (Revenue lead) + COO or CEO sign-off for any cap > $2M. Markus — if you want to route to General Counsel for final sign-off I'm fine to loop.

Aditya
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — after reviewing the risk summary and commercial upside, I approve the one-time exception with the following mandatory conditions:

1) Cap: Approve pilot liability cap up to $3M for the 12-month pilot only. The contract must include an explicit clause that reverts the cap to our standard $1M upon any renewal or extension without a new signed exception.

2) Warranty carveout: Approve a narrowly tailored carveout limited to third-party data ingestion where Crestview is the sole source and control of the third-party component. Any failure traceable to Redwood services, integrations, or our delivery will remain covered.

3) Commercial offset: Approve a maximum discount of 15% (not 25%). If the customer insists on a deeper commercial concession, return to me with a compensation plan (e.g., success-based pricing or milestone credits).

4) Risk acceptance memo: Aditya, please prepare a 1-page risk acceptance memo that summarizes residual risks and remediation steps; route to me and Markus for signature and file with the deal record.

5) Executive visibility: I want CFO and COO notified before signature; Marissa, copy finance@redwood.com when you send the final SOW.

With those conditions, proceed — get the signed SOW by 2026-11-20. If Crestview refuses the 15% cap on discount, hold and escalate.
